from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Music is organized by steady pulses called beats.", "A measure is a container for musical time.", "Time signatures define the rhythm of the music."]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Heartbeat of Music", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors per lecture line
        colors = ["#FF00FF", "#00FFFF", "#FFFF00"]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Pulse visualization
        self.lecture[0].set_color(colors[0])
        dot = Dot(color=colors[0]).scale(2)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'C3')
        
        # Simple pulse animation
        pulse = Circle(radius=0.5, color=colors[0]).move_to(dot.get_center())
        self.add(pulse)
        self.play(Create(dot), FadeIn(pulse), run_time=1)
        self.play(pulse.animate.scale(2).set_opacity(0), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(colors[1])
        # Container (Measure) representation
        container = Rectangle(height=2, width=4, color=colors[1])
        self.place_at_grid(container, 'D4')
        self.play(Create(container), run_time=1)
        
        # Add rhythmic indicators inside
        ticks = VGroup(*[Line(UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5, color=colors[1]) for _ in range(4)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8)
        ticks.move_to(container.get_center())
        self.play(Create(ticks), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(colors[2])
        # Time Signature: "4/4"
        ts = MathTex(r"\frac{4}{4}", color=colors[2]).scale(2)
        self.place_at_grid(ts, 'B2')
        self.play(Write(ts), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Anatomy of a Measure (Time Signatures)", [
            "Time signatures look like fractions in math.",
            "The top number counts beats per measure.",
            "The bottom number defines the note value."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw a simple 4/4 time signature fraction. (Color: #FFFFFF)
        time_sig = MathTex(r"{\frac{4}{4}}", font_size=96, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(time_sig, 'B2', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(time_sig))
        self.wait(2)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Partition a circle into 4 equal rhythmic segments. (Color: #00FF00)
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE)
        lines = VGroup(*[Line(ORIGIN, 1.5*RIGHT).rotate(i * PI/2, about_point=ORIGIN) for i in range(4)])
        pie_chart = VGroup(circle, lines)
        self.place_at_grid(pie_chart, 'E4', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(Create(circle), Create(lines))
        for line in lines:
            line.set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(2)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the first beat as the downbeat. (Color: #FF0000)
        # Assuming the first segment is top-right (0 to PI/2)
        downbeat = Sector(radius=1.5, start_angle=0, angle=PI/2, color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(downbeat, 'E4', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(downbeat))
        self.wait(2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Notes represent fractions of a musical measure.",
            "Whole notes equal one full measure capacity.",
            "Quarter notes represent one-fourth of the measure.",
            "Combining notes must sum to the measure total.",
            "Mathematics ensures notes perfectly fill each measure."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Division of Time", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        whole_note = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE).set_fill(WHITE, opacity=0.3)
        half_note_1 = Circle(radius=0.35, color="#FFFF00").set_fill("#FFFF00", opacity=0.3)
        half_note_2 = Circle(radius=0.35, color="#FFFF00").set_fill("#FFFF00", opacity=0.3)
        
        q1 = Circle(radius=0.25, color="#00FFFF").set_fill("#00FFFF", opacity=0.3)
        q2 = Circle(radius=0.25, color="#00FFFF").set_fill("#00FFFF", opacity=0.3)
        q3 = Circle(radius=0.25, color="#00FFFF").set_fill("#00FFFF", opacity=0.3)
        q4 = Circle(radius=0.25, color="#00FFFF").set_fill("#00FFFF", opacity=0.3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(whole_note, "B2")
        self.add(whole_note)
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Split into half notes
        self.remove(whole_note)
        self.place_at_grid(half_note_1, "B1")
        self.place_at_grid(half_note_2, "B3")
        self.add(half_note_1, half_note_2)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.remove(half_note_1, half_note_2)
        self.place_at_grid(q1, "B1")
        self.place_at_grid(q2, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(q3, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(q4, "B4")
        self.add(q1, q2, q3, q4)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FF00FF")
        # Visualizing eighth notes (just as smaller circles)
        e1 = Circle(radius=0.15, color="#FF00FF").set_fill("#FF00FF", opacity=0.3)
        e2 = Circle(radius=0.15, color="#FF00FF").set_fill("#FF00FF", opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(e1, "C1")
        self.place_at_grid(e2, "C2")
        self.add(e1, e2)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(3)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Complex Meters and Syncopation", [
            "Compound meters use groups of three beats.",
            "Math allows us to accent specific beats.",
            "Syncopation creates rhythm by shifting musical stress."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a 7/8 time signature meter structure. (Color: #FFCC00)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFCC00")
        beats = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color="#FFCC00") for _ in range(7)])
        beats.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(beats, 'B1', 'B6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(beats)
        self.wait(4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight syncopated off-beat accents. (Color: #FF6600)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF6600")
        accents = VGroup(*[Star(outer_radius=0.25, inner_radius=0.1, color="#FF6600") for _ in [0, 3, 5]])
        self.place_at_grid(accents[0], 'D2')
        self.place_at_grid(accents[1], 'D4')
        self.place_at_grid(accents[2], 'D6')
        self.add(accents)
        self.wait(4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Visualize irregular grouping patterns in time. (Color: #33CCFF)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#33CCFF")
        pattern = VGroup(
            Rectangle(height=0.5, width=1.0, color="#33CCFF"),
            Rectangle(height=0.5, width=1.5, color="#33CCFF"),
            Rectangle(height=0.5, width=1.0, color="#33CCFF")
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(pattern, 'E1', 'E6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(pattern)
        self.wait(4)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Measure theory acts as grammar for composers.",
            "Different parts must share a numerical structure.",
            "Synchronization creates harmony through shared rhythm."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Composer’s Equation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        notes = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(4)])
        notes.arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(notes, "B3")
        
        measure_label = MathTex(r"1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 1").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(measure_label, "D3")
        
        rhythm_formula = MathTex(r"T = \sum_{i=1}^{n} d_i").scale(1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(rhythm_formula, "E3")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#99FF33"))
        self.play(FadeIn(notes))
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF9933"))
        self.play(Write(measure_label))
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#CC99FF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(rhythm_formula))
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Rhythm of Mathematics: Understanding Music and Measure Theory
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in music theory and STEM

sections.title: Introduction: The Heartbeat of Music
sections.content: Define 'Measure' as a vessel for time. Introduce the pulse (beat) and the concept of time signatures as fractional constraints on musical flow.
sections.example: Visualize a robotic drummer 'Tic-Toc' hitting a drum at a steady, constant interval, defining the basic 'pulse'.

sections.title: The Anatomy of a Measure (Time Signatures)
sections.content: Explain the time signature fraction. The top number represents 'beats per measure' (numerator), and the bottom number represents the 'note value' that gets one beat (denominator).
sections.example: Show a 4/4 time signature. A visual animation of a 'pizza pie' cut into 4 slices; each measure must hold exactly one whole pie's worth of notes.

sections.title: Mathematical Division of Time
sections.content: Prerequisite: Basic fractions. Connect note lengths (Whole, Half, Quarter, Eighth) to powers of 2 (1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Show how they sum up to equal the measure capacity.
sections.example: Animated 'Tetris' blocks falling into a measure box: two quarter notes (1/4 + 1/4) plus one half note (1/2) perfectly filling the 4/4 container.

sections.title: Complex Meters and Syncopation
sections.content: Introduce compound meters (e.g., 6/8) to show how division isn't always linear. Explain that math in music allows for 'stress' (accents) on specific beats.
sections.example: A group of squirrels gathering nuts: they dance in groups of three (1-2-3, 1-2-3), illustrating the 'swing' or 'triplet' feel compared to the standard binary count.

sections.title: Application: The Composer’s Equation
sections.content: Summarize how measure theory acts as the 'grammar' for music, allowing different instruments to synchronize perfectly through shared numerical structures.
sections.example: Display a split-screen: A pianist and a violinist playing different melodies, but their 'measure bars' align perfectly like synchronized gears in a clock.
